newsitem.title: UK: Celltech up on U.S. antibody patent news.
newsitem.headline: Celltech up on U.S. antibody patent news.

text.p: Shares in UK biotech specialist Celltech Group Plc gained over two percent on Thursday after it said the U.S. patent office had granted a key patent covering certain forms of artificially-created human antibodies.
Celltech rose as high as 520p but slipped back to trade at 512-1/2p by 0850 GMT, up 12-1/2p on the day. Some 165,000 shares had changed hands. The broader market was steady at the time.

Celltech said the patent, which lasts until 2014, will "substantially extend" the protection of products which it is developing using antibodies, and should lead to royalties from other companies using Celltech technology.

Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum said royalty payments from the latest patent award "could come through in the next three years" given the number of late-stage antibody products in the U.S.
But he said it was difficult to put a precise monetary value on the new patent, with Celltech likely to agree to technology swaps with companies that turn out to be infringing it.
Analysts said the Celltech's share rise may partly reflect the relative lack of recent news from the company. News of progress on its lead drugs is expected before the year-end.
